intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive dilated cardiomyopathy-2A (CMD2A) is caused by homozygous mutation in the gene encoding cardiac troponin I (TNNI3; 191044) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive dilated cardiomyopathy-2A (CMD2A) is caused by homozygous mutation in the TNNI3 gene, which encodes cardiac troponin I.
checks.evidence_quote: TNNI3 is the first recessive gene identified for this condition, and we suggest that other such genes could be pinpointed by mutation analyses designed to identify homozygous mutations.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports recessive dilated cardiomyopathy caused by a TNNI3 mutation. It does not state outright that the mutation was homozygous, and it does not use the name CMD2A.

checks.claim: The TNNI3 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no chromosomal location for TNNI3.

paragraphs.text: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a disorder of the heart muscle. The left ventricle, or both ventricles, become enlarged and pump poorly, which leads to congestive heart failure and arrhythmias and can cause early death. CMD2A is an autosomal recessive form of idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy caused by mutation in the cardiac troponin I gene.

checks.claim: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a disorder of the heart muscle.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not define dilated cardiomyopathy as a disorder of the heart muscle.

checks.claim: In dilated cardiomyopathy, the left ventricle or both ventricles become enlarged and pump poorly.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not describe ventricular enlargement or poor pumping.

checks.claim: Dilated cardiomyopathy leads to congestive heart failure and arrhythmias.
checks.evidence_quote: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy is a common cause of heart failure.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions heart failure but not arrhythmias.

checks.claim: Dilated cardiomyopathy can cause early death.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not mention early death.

checks.claim: CMD2A is an autosomal recessive form of idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a recessive form of idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. The name CMD2A is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: CMD2A is caused by mutation in the cardiac troponin I gene (TNNI3).
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
checks.explanation: The disease is attributed to a mutation in TNNI3, the gene for cardiac troponin I.

paragraphs.text: Murphy et al. (2004) established autosomal recessive inheritance of CMD2A. In their family, affected individuals were homozygous for a TNNI3 mutation, and heterozygous carriers were clinically unaffected.

checks.claim: Murphy et al. (2004) established autosomal recessive inheritance of CMD2A.
checks.evidence_quote: TNNI3 is the first recessive gene identified for this condition
checks.explanation: The paper reports recessive inheritance in the family it studied.

checks.claim: In the CMD2A family studied by Murphy et al. (2004), affected individuals were homozygous for a TNNI3 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: we suggest that other such genes could be pinpointed by mutation analyses designed to identify homozygous mutations.
checks.explanation: Homozygosity is implied by the recessive disease and the mention of homozygous mutations, but the abstract never states that affected members were homozygous.

checks.claim: In the CMD2A family studied by Murphy et al. (2004), heterozygous carriers of the TNNI3 mutation were clinically unaffected.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention heterozygous carriers or their clinical status; this detail may be in the full text.

paragraphs.text: Dilated cardiomyopathy is genetically heterogeneous, and most forms are inherited as autosomal dominant traits. In other reports, heterozygous mutations in TNNI3 have also been associated with dominantly inherited dilated cardiomyopathy and with hypertrophic and restrictive cardiomyopathy.

checks.claim: Dilated cardiomyopathy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: More than 30 loci have been identified, several of which encode sarcomeric proteins which can also be mutated to cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper reports more than 30 loci, which shows the disease is genetically heterogeneous.

checks.claim: Most forms of dilated cardiomyopathy are inherited as autosomal dominant traits.
checks.evidence_quote: Idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is inherited in approximately one third of cases, usually as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.explanation: The paper says inherited DCM is usually autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in TNNI3 have been associated with dominantly inherited dilated cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: These are the first reported autosomal dominant DCM-causing mutations in TNNI3
checks.explanation: The paper reports TNNI3 missense mutations in autosomal dominant familial DCM. The abstract doesn't use the word 'heterozygous', but dominant inheritance implies it.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in TNNI3 have been associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: One contractile protein gene well known as a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy disease gene, but with no reported mutation in autosomal dominant DCM, is TNNI3 which encodes cardiac troponin I.
checks.explanation: The paper states that TNNI3 is a known hypertrophic cardiomyopathy gene.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in TNNI3 have been associated with restrictive cardiomyopathy.
checks.explanation: The abstract doesn't mention restrictive cardiomyopathy.

paragraphs.text: Murphy et al. (2004) studied a family with recessively inherited idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. In affected members they identified a homozygous ala2-to-val (A2V) mutation in the TNNI3 gene. Heterozygous family members were unaffected. In functional studies, the mutation weakened the interaction of cardiac troponin I with cardiac troponin T.

checks.claim: Murphy et al. (2004) studied a family with recessively inherited idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes a family with recessive idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy.

checks.claim: Affected members of the family studied by Murphy et al. (2004) were homozygous for an ala2-to-val (A2V) mutation in the TNNI3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not name the A2V variant and only implies homozygosity; the specific variant is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: Family members heterozygous for the TNNI3 A2V mutation were unaffected.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe the clinical status of heterozygous family members.

checks.claim: In functional studies, the TNNI3 A2V mutation weakened the interaction of cardiac troponin I with cardiac troponin T.
checks.evidence_quote: Functional studies showed impairment of troponin interactions that could lead to diminished myocardial contractility.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports impaired troponin interactions but does not say that troponin T was the partner affected.

paragraphs.text: Murphy et al. (2004) found an ala2-to-val (A2V) mutation in the TNNI3 gene in homozygous state in affected members of a family with autosomal recessive idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. Heterozygous carriers were unaffected. Functional studies showed that the mutation impaired the binding of troponin I to troponin T.

checks.claim: Murphy et al. (2004) found the TNNI3 ala2-to-val (A2V) mutation in homozygous state in affected members of a family with autosomal recessive idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel TNNI3 mutation in a family with recessive disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not name the A2V variant and does not explicitly state that affected members were homozygous.

checks.claim: Heterozygous carriers of the TNNI3 A2V mutation were unaffected.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention heterozygous carriers.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed that the TNNI3 A2V mutation impaired the binding of troponin I to troponin T.
checks.evidence_quote: Functional studies showed impairment of troponin interactions that could lead to diminished myocardial contractility.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports impaired troponin interactions in general; binding of troponin I to troponin T is not specified.

references.label: Murphy et al. (2004)
references.citation: Murphy RT, Mogensen J, Shaw A, Kubo T, Hughes S, McKenna WJ. Novel mutation in cardiac troponin I in recessive idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy. Lancet 363: 371-2, 2004. [PubMed: 15070570]
